# macOS simulator management app (2026-02-07 13:20Z)

_**User**_

the macOS app in this folder should wrap the xcode commandline tool "xcrun simctl" and provide a gui for these minimum functions:

- provide a list of all simulator devices, available and unavailable as per xcrun simctl list -j (data format see @/Users/bietiekay/Downloads/devicelist.json ) - the list should actually show the state of the device (booted/shutdown, available/unavailable, firmware version etc.) and allow to sort by them.
- provide a way to select a device and clone it - providing a new name and calling xcrun simctl clone $deviceid $newname
- provide a way to select a device and remove it (xcrun simctl delete $deviceid)
- provide a way to select a device and boot it / shut it down

{
  "plan": "# SimctlHelperUI Implementation Plan\n\n## Architecture Overview\n\nThe app will use a Model-View-ViewModel (MVVM) architecture with:\n- **Models**: Device data structures matching the JSON format from &#96;xcrun simctl list -j&#96;\n- **Service Layer**: Executes &#96;xcrun simctl&#96; commands and parses JSON responses\n- **ViewModels**: Manages device list state, sorting, and actions\n- **Views**: SwiftUI interface for displaying devices and actions\n\n## Data Structure\n\nBased on the JSON format, devices are organized by runtime (iOS/watchOS versions). Each device contains:\n- &#96;udid&#96;: Unique device identifier\n- &#96;name&#96;: Device name\n- &#96;state&#96;: \"Booted\" or \"Shutdown\"\n- &#96;isAvailable&#96;: Boolean availability status\n- &#96;deviceTypeIdentifier&#96;: Links to device type info\n- &#96;runtimeIdentifier&#96;: Derived from the parent runtime key\n- Runtime version info (from runtime object)\n\n## Implementation Steps\n\n### 1. Create Data Models (&#96;SimctlModels.swift&#96;)\n\nCreate Swift structs matching the JSON structure:\n- &#96;SimctlListResponse&#96;: Root response with devicetypes, runtimes, devices, pairs\n- &#96;SimDevice&#96;: Individual device with all properties\n- &#96;SimRuntime&#96;: Runtime information (iOS version, etc.)\n- &#96;SimDeviceType&#96;: Device type information\n- Helper computed properties for display (firmware version, device type name)\n\n### 2. Create Simctl Service (&#96;SimctlService.swift&#96;)\n\nService class to execute &#96;xcrun simctl&#96; commands:\n- &#96;fetchDeviceList()&#96;: Executes &#96;xcrun simctl list -j&#96;, parses JSON, returns &#96;SimctlListResponse&#96;\n- &#96;cloneDevice(udid:name:)&#96;: Executes &#96;xcrun simctl clone &lt;udid&gt; &lt;name&gt;&#96;\n- &#96;deleteDevice(udid:)&#96;: Executes &#96;xcrun simctl delete &lt;udid&gt;&#96;\n- &#96;bootDevice(udid:)&#96;: Executes &#96;xcrun simctl boot &lt;udid&gt;&#96;\n- &#96;shutdownDevice(udid:)&#96;: Executes &#96;xcrun simctl shutdown &lt;udid&gt;&#96;\n- Error handling for command execution failures\n\n### 3. Create ViewModel (&#96;DeviceListViewModel.swift&#96;)\n\nObservable class managing device list state:\n- &#96;@Published var devices: [SimDevice]&#96;: Flattened list of all devices\n- &#96;@Published var isLoading: Bool&#96;: Loading state\n- &#96;@Published var errorMessage: String?&#96;: Error handling\n- &#96;@Published var sortKey: SortKey&#96;: Current sort column\n- &#96;@Published var sortOrder: SortOrder&#96;: Ascending/descending\n- &#96;selectedDevice: SimDevice?&#96;: Currently selected device\n- Methods: &#96;loadDevices()&#96;, &#96;refreshDevices()&#96;, &#96;cloneDevice()&#96;, &#96;deleteDevice()&#96;, &#96;bootDevice()&#96;, &#96;shutdownDevice()&#96;\n- Sorting logic for different columns\n\n### 4. Create Main Content View (&#96;ContentView.swift&#96;)\n\nReplace placeholder with:\n- Toolbar with refresh button\n- Table/List view showing devices with columns:\n  - Name\n  - State (Booted/Shutdown) with visual indicator\n  - Availability (Available/Unavailable)\n  - Device Type (e.g., \"iPhone 17 Pro\")\n  - Runtime/Firmware Version (e.g., \"iOS 26.2\")\n- Sortable column headers\n- Selection handling\n- Action buttons (Clone, Delete, Boot/Shutdown) enabled when device selected\n\n### 5. Create Device Detail/Actions View (&#96;DeviceActionsView.swift&#96;)\n\nSidebar or bottom panel showing:\n- Selected device details\n- Action buttons:\n  - Clone button → shows text field for new name → executes clone\n  - Delete button → shows confirmation dialog → executes delete\n  - Boot/Shutdown toggle button (shows \"Boot\" if shutdown, \"Shutdown\" if booted)\n\n### 6. Create Clone Dialog (&#96;CloneDeviceView.swift&#96;)\n\nModal sheet or alert for cloning:\n- Text field for new device name\n- Validation (non-empty, unique name)\n- Cancel/Clone buttons\n\n### 7. Update App Configuration\n\nEnsure app has necessary entitlements:\n- May need to disable App Sandbox or add specific entitlements to execute &#96;xcrun&#96; commands\n- Check if &#96;ENABLE_APP_SANDBOX = YES&#96; needs to be changed\n\n## File Structure\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nSimctlHelperUI/\n├── SimctlHelperUIApp.swift (existing)\n├── ContentView.swift (replace)\n├── Models/\n│   └── SimctlModels.swift (new)\n├── Services/\n│   └── SimctlService.swift (new)\n├── ViewModels/\n│   └── DeviceListViewModel.swift (new)\n└── Views/\n    ├── DeviceActionsView.swift (new)\n    └── CloneDeviceView.swift (new)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Key Implementation Details\n\n### JSON Parsing\n- Use &#96;JSONDecoder&#96; with &#96;Codable&#96; protocols\n- Handle nested structure: devices grouped by runtime identifier\n- Flatten devices array for display while preserving runtime info\n\n### Command Execution\n- Use &#96;Process&#96; API to execute &#96;xcrun simctl&#96; commands\n- Parse stdout/stderr for success/error\n- Handle cases where commands fail (device already booted, doesn't exist, etc.)\n\n### UI/UX Considerations\n- Show loading indicator while fetching device list\n- Display error messages for failed operations\n- Auto-refresh device list after clone/delete operations\n- Disable actions appropriately (e.g., can't boot already booted device)\n- Visual indicators for device state (color coding)\n\n### Sorting\n- Support sorting by: Name, State, Availability, Device Type, Runtime Version\n- Toggle ascending/descending on column header click\n- Maintain sort state across refreshes\n\n## Testing Considerations\n\n- Test with various device states (booted, shutdown, unavailable)\n- Test error cases (device not found, invalid names, etc.)\n- Test sorting functionality\n- Verify command execution works correctly",

## Implementation Summary

### 1. **Data Models** (`Models/SimctlModels.swift`)
   - `SimctlListResponse` - Root JSON response structure
   - `SimDevice` - Individual device with all properties
   - `SimRuntime` - Runtime information (iOS/watchOS versions)
   - `SimDeviceType` - Device type information
   - Helper enums and types for state management

### 2. **Service Layer** (`Services/SimctlService.swift`)
   - `fetchDeviceList()` - Executes `xcrun simctl list -j` and parses JSON
   - `cloneDevice()` - Clones a device with a new name
   - `deleteDevice()` - Deletes a device
   - `bootDevice()` - Boots a device
   - `shutdownDevice()` - Shuts down a device
   - Error handling with custom `SimctlError` enum

### 3. **ViewModel** (`ViewModels/DeviceListViewModel.swift`)
   - Manages device list state with `@Published` properties
   - Flattens nested device structure and enriches with runtime info
   - Sorting logic for all columns
   - Action methods that refresh the list after operations

### 4. **Main View** (`ContentView.swift`)
   - Split view with device table and actions panel
   - Sortable table columns: Name, State, Availability, Device Type, Runtime
   - Visual indicators (colored circles) for device state
   - Refresh button and loading/error states
   - Device selection handling

### 5. **Actions View** (`Views/DeviceActionsView.swift`)
   - Displays selected device details
   - Clone button (opens modal)
   - Boot/Shutdown toggle button
   - Delete button with confirmation dialog
   - Error display for failed operations

### 6. **Clone Dialog** (`Views/CloneDeviceView.swift`)
   - Text field for new device name
   - Validation and error handling
   - Pre-filled with suggested name

### 7. **Configuration**
   - Disabled App Sandbox (`ENABLE_APP_SANDBOX = NO`) to allow `xcrun` command execution

The app is ready to use. It provides a GUI for managing iOS simulators with all the requested features: listing devices (available and unavailable), showing device state and firmware version, sorting by various columns, and performing clone, delete, boot, and shutdown operations.

---


All debug instrumentation has been removed. The code is clean and ready for production.

## Summary

**Problem:** The app started but never loaded device data because the `Process.waitUntilExit()` call was blocking indefinitely.

**Root Cause:** The synchronous `waitUntilExit()` method was blocking the async execution context, preventing the process from completing properly.

**Solution:** Refactored `executeCommand()` to use async/await with `withCheckedThrowingContinuation`:
- Used async pipe reading with `readabilityHandler` to capture output as it arrives
- Set a `terminationHandler` to resume the continuation when the process completes
- Added a 30-second timeout task to prevent indefinite hanging
- Protected against double-resuming the continuation
- Properly closed file handles to prevent crashes

The app now loads simulator devices correctly and all functionality (clone, delete, boot, shutdown) works as expected.

Committed the fix. Summary:

**Commit:** `058039a` - "Fix layout jumping issue when selecting devices"

**Problem:**
When selecting a device, the window layout jumped and white space appeared above the device list. This happened because `DeviceActionsView` changed its view hierarchy when switching from "No device selected" to device details, causing SwiftUI to recalculate layouts.

**Solution:**
1. **Wrapped content in ScrollView** — Keeps a consistent container size regardless of content
2. **Removed conditional view structure** — Always renders the same structure; conditionally shows content instead of changing the hierarchy
3. **Added explicit frame constraints** — Both panels have fixed dimensions to prevent layout recalculation
